title: Pretraining
description: Training a model from scratch on raw text using next-token prediction.
whenToUse: You want to create a new foundation model or train on a completely new language/domain.
whyNotOthers: Most expensive and data-hungry. Only choose when fine-tuning cannot achieve your goal.
dataRequired: Billions to trillions of tokens. Cleaned, deduplicated, filtered text.
hardware: Multi-GPU (8+ H100/A100) for models >1B. Single GPU for <100M parameter models.

title: Continued Pretraining
description: Continuing to train an existing model on new data to expand its knowledge or adapt to a new domain.
whenToUse: You have domain-specific text and want the model to learn new facts/patterns without changing its basic behavior.
whyNotOthers: Better than fine-tuning when the new data is large (millions of tokens) and similar in format to pretraining data.
dataRequired: Millions to billions of tokens of domain text.
hardware: Similar to pretraining but can start with fewer GPUs if model is frozen except last layers.

title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
description: Training a model on input-output pairs to teach it to follow instructions.
whenToUse: You want the model to respond in a specific format or follow instructions for a specific task.
whyNotOthers: Use SFT when you have labeled examples. Use continued pretraining when you have raw domain text.
dataRequired: Thousands to hundreds of thousands of instruction-response pairs.
hardware: Single GPU (with LoRA) to multi-GPU (full fine-tuning).

title: LoRA
description: Low-Rank Adaptation: freeze the base model and train small rank-decomposition matrices attached to selected layers.
whenToUse: GPU memory is limited but you want better results than prompt engineering. The standard approach for fine-tuning.
whyNotOthers: Slightly less capable than full fine-tuning, but uses ~10x less memory. Choose full FT only if you have the hardware.
dataRequired: Similar to SFT: thousands to hundreds of thousands of examples.
hardware: Single consumer GPU (24GB) for 7B models. Multi-GPU for larger models.

title: QLoRA
description: LoRA combined with 4-bit quantization of the base model. Enables fine-tuning 7B models on a single 8GB GPU.
whenToUse: You have very limited GPU memory (8-12GB) but want to fine-tune a large model.
whyNotOthers: Slightly lower quality than full LoRA due to quantization noise. But often good enough, and dramatically cheaper.

title: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
description: Align model behavior using preference pairs instead of training a separate reward model.
whenToUse: You have preference data (chosen/rejected responses) and want to align the model without RL.
whyNotOthers: Simpler than RLHF (no reward model, no PPO). But requires preference data which is harder to collect than instruction data.
dataRequired: Preference pairs: (chosen_response, rejected_response) for many prompts.

title: RLHF
description: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. Train a reward model, then optimize the LLM with PPO.
whenToUse: You need the most sophisticated alignment. The original InstructGPT/ChatGPT approach.
whyNotOthers: Much more complex than DPO. Three models needed (LLM, reward, reference) instead of DPO's two. DPO is usually sufficient.
dataRequired: ranked responses for reward model training + preference data for RL.
hardware: More GPUs than DPO (need room for reward model + reference model).
